properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/30/2020
Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 900854
Permit API: 131-20562
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/30/2020
Comments: On site Monday (11/30/20) for the start up of Step Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs). There are (5) wells on this pad, they are the Hunter 5H, 6H, 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC. All (5) wells were in production. The (9x5), (13x9) and the (20x13) annuli of all the wells are plumbed to surface w/ rubber lines, the (20x13) annuli are venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are sharing a 2" vent line to the production tanks. All annuli have transponders installed and are being monitored by the Operator. The ball valves were closed on all (20x13) annuli vents before there common vent line in order to isolate each annuli individually for gas checks being performed today for the beginning of the (SPBUTs).- Operator rep. (Tom Vitella) was on site to shut in the (20x13) annuli. - An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal.11/12/20) was turned on and gas checks performed @ the (20x13) Sentry valves showed no gas at time of shut in. - The (20x13) annuli were shut in @ 10:00, marking the start of the (SPBUTs). End of testing will be on Thurs. (12/3/20).

Comments: This inspection is being performed following the operator report of a production water leak at the Potato Creek Pad A this morning. The spill was initially reported by the water hauler.This is a producing Utica shale well pad, with two producing wells on it. The operator has gas production units on site, as well as a tank battery with two 400 barrel tanks. It appears as though a water truck was picking up production water at 7 am this morning, and some water was spilled on site. The area impacted is approximately 25 feet long and 5-10 feet wide. Based on the visual inspection, it appears as though approximately 10 gallons was spilled. The operator intends to have a mini excavator on site shortly, which will be used to clean up this spill and remove impacted soil. As this spill is low volume and all contained to a small area, all violations are considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2017-01-03 to Rice Drilling B Llc in Somerset Twp, Washington county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Rice Drilling B Llc
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2017-01-03
Violation Code 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID 776266
Permit API 125-27782
Unconventional Y
County Washington
Municipality Somerset Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2017-01-03
Comments On January 3, 2017, I inspected the Papa Bear well site accompanied by OGI Supervisor Scott Sabocheck, OGI Eric Peterson, and OGI John Rushin as well as a number of Rice Energy representatives in response to a fire and subsequent loss of brine and other fluids to the pad that occurred on 1/1/17. Observations from the inspection are below. •At the stream crossing on the site access road substantial amounts of gravel and mud had been sprayed over the CFS and into the immediate area of the stream. The issue was communicated to site personnel at the time of inspection and immediate actions were taken to remediate. No violation at this time. •The fire and associated efforts to extinguish it resulted in currently unknown amounts of brine, oil, firefighting chemicals, and other pollutants reaching the surface of the pad via numerous holes burned in the liner. This constitutes a violation of 25 Pa. Code § 78.57(a) and 25 Pa. Code § 78.54 in that production fluids were spilled to the ground. •At the time of inspection the operator requested that the DEP consider if fracking could be completed before full remediation and expressed intent to partially remediate the spilled material as soon as possible by cutting out and repairing the damaged liner and removing the bulk of the spilled and affected materials in the immediate area. •Documentation of events, full chemical details, and remediation plans were requested from the operator at the time of inspection. •Particular concerns were expressed and discussed regarding potential impacts and toxicity of foaming agents used in fire suppression.

ID: 776265 Date: 2017-01-03 00:00:00 Type: Environmental Health & Safety

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/18/2021 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/18/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 911088
Permit API: 015-23648
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/18/2021
Comments: On 03/18/2021, Department of Environmental Protection representative John Ciccone (Water Quality Specialist) conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) MAGGIE location in response to a spill notification (Complaint ID # 355355). Eric Hottenstein (CALLC HSE Supervisor) reported the release at 0700 hours on 03/18/2021. Mr. Hottenstein’s initial report stated that he was notified that an estimated 100 gallons of Blue Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF), an additive for diesel fuel, was spilled onto the western side of the pad surface. According to the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) on DEF, the substance is a mixture of 67.5% water and 32.5% urea by weight (photo # 9). The spill occurred when a 400-gallon tote of DEF was punctured by a forklift while repositioning the tote onto containment. Fluid that was pooled on the pad surface was vacuumed up and impacted soils were excavated. Excavated soils were placed within containment. I arrived onsite at 1051 hours. The weather was 43 degrees with steady rainfall. CALLC crews were present onsite and preparing for stimulation operations, scheduled to begin today (03/18/2021). I checked in with Brent Thomas (CALLC Safety Manager) to announce my presence and in order to be guided to the release location. I observed 2 separate containments, each approximately 12 feet x 12 feet in dimension, that excavated soils were staged within (photo # 1, 2). Excavated soils were covered with tarp, and containments had berms present. A vacuum truck was parked at the location of release at the time of my arrival (photo # 3). Mr. Thomas instructed to truck to move so I could gather observations. According to photographs of the initial release, an area of approximately 20 feet x 20 feet was impacted (photo # 15). During the time of this inspection, the area was covered puddles and was not covered with containment (photo # 4). No staining on the pad surface or odors were noted at this time. Field measured specific conductivity readings were taken from puddles within the area of release and readings ranged from ~ 250 – 600 uS/cm (photo # 5, 6). Due to the solubility of DEF in water, I recommended to Mr. Thomas that it may be prudent to cover the area with containment or additional timber matting. Creston Environmental is scheduled to collect soil samples for Act 2 remediation purposes, but a specific date for collection was not provided. The release of an estimated 100 gallons of DEF to the pad surface is in violation of the Pennsylvania Clean Streams Law Section 402b, the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) ("Temporary Storage"). Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23648. Due to the quantity of DEF released onto the pad surface, this release is referred to the DEP's Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. I departed the site at 1142 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 957718
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: On 3/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4000998, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4 and 6). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 5 and 7). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 10 and 11). Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photo 2).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4000998 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: On June 14, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline and Rob Marquez conducted a routine site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The recently constructed access road and well pad has sparse vegetation growth occurring. The DEP recommends reseeding the site to prevent areas from eroding. An erosion rill has developed through the plunge pool on Culvert 7. The rill has washed sediment between two compost filter socks and off the LOD of the site. The DEP recommends adding and expanding stone to the downgrade side of the plunge pool to create a more gradual and level runoff and to slow the velocity of the flow. During the inspection, the plunge pool at culvert 9 was still being overwhelmed from the flow of water through the culvert. The DEP recommends excavating the sediment that has built up at the stacked filter socks. When the sediment has been excavated and the stacked filter socks have been dewatered, the DEP recommends removing the stacked filter socks. The filter sock that is located on the top of the plunge is recommended to be removed and to bring the level of stone up to the same level as the culvert outlet. At the time of inspection, the level of the plunge pool appears to be a foot lower than the culvert outlet. More stone is recommended to be added to create a more level overflow of the plunge pool which will slow the velocity of the water. The slope toe key drain outlet prior to Culvert No. 9 is flowing over the compost filter sock. The compost filter sock still appeared to be in place. The DEP recommends monitoring this area and replacing or repairing the compost filter sock as necessary. A seep has recently caused some erosion rills near the well pad entrance. The DEP recommends addressing the erosion rills and the seep. A channel has been dug to direct the seep towards the diversion berm. The sediment leaving the LOD at Culvert 7 is a violation of of Chapter 102.4(b)1 and Chapter 102.11(a)1.

Comments: On 8/25/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well received on 8/18/2026.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- A rig is staged on site for plugging operations. A dark, oily fluid was observed at one of the plugging rig controls. The Department recommends that the Operator monitor this portion of the plugging rig and take necessary measures to prevent a fluid release to the ground.- The access road and well site are heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. No site stabilization measures, such as gravel, have been implemented anywhere on site.- It appears that no perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were installed on site prior to starting earth disturbances related to well plugging operations. No E and S/Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.- No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas well. The API number was not observed on site.- The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site. The Department recommends that the Operator post their information on site in accordance with OGA 3211(G), until plugging operations are complete and the Certificate of Well Plugging (COWP) is approved by DEP Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.While on site, the Department spoke via phone with Operator representative Chris Caskey and informed them of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations in this inspection report. The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection at the SWEPI LP - Houck 433 well pad located in Shippen Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/11/2019 @1130 hours. Matt Skolny, SWEPI LP was present on the pony pad for the spill investigation. Morgan Davis, SWEPI LP OSR was present on the main pad. The weather was 37 degrees, sunny, winds WNW 15mph, the previously deposited snow is melting causing the site to the very muddy with standing water. April Heater, SWEPI LP reported a spill to the DEP's regional office on 3/8/2019 @1500 hours. Onsite personnel were breaking apart the "fastline", which was used to carry frack fluid from the AST on the pony pad to the main pad. Mr. Skolny stated they had run a number of courses of freshwater through the line to clean it out. When the line was dismantled the open end was placed in a tub, on secondary containment, on the NW corner of the pony pad. No fluid came out initially, but when the onsite personnel left to work on another area, fluid was discharged from the end of the pipe. The fluid overtopped containment, and entered the channel in the NW corner of the pad. SWEPI estimated `20 gallons of fluid was released into containent with `20 gallons overtopping and discharging into the perimeter E&S ditch. As of today's inspection, a tub of icy, black, frozen/slush mix that was initially recovered from the channel had a field measured conductivity of 3.0 mS/cm. This tub was placed on secondary containment for disposal. The channel off the edge of the pad was full of ice/snow with a small volume of liquid. No elevated conductivity was measured in the ditch or in puddles on the corner of the pony pad. A black greasy material and oily sheen was observed in the NW corner of the ditch. SWEPI was notified and instructed to have the material removed from the ditch. Matt Bailey was present onsite at this point, and stated he would have the remaining issues addressed. Due to the reported release of fluids onto the ground surface, violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a56(a) Temporary Storage SWMA 301 Solid Waste Management Act CSL 402(b) Potential Pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth An inspection of the main pad was also conducted. The coil rig was observed drilling out plugs on the 6H well on the main pad. Mr. Davis, SWEPI OSR accompanied me around the well pad during the inspection. A few areas of elevated conductivity were discovered inside containment. Mr. Davis stated he would have the fluid removed when the vac truck returned to the site. Mr. Davis was also notified of containment berms that appeared broken/smashed and were in need of repair. Although the site was very muddy, with large amounts of standing water, none of the puddles on the pad surface were found to have elevated conductivity. The E&S trap and rock-lined channels appeared frozen. No sedimentation or erosion was observed. I departed the site at 1345 hours.

Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Inspection Date: 4/06/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa. Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8226732
Permit API: 129-26623
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2025
Comments: On March 25, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the Wissinger 001 Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department at 10:25 am of an explosion at the well site. Present during the inspection were several representatives from Kriebel including Shane Kriebel, Jay Niehenke, Ronald Seich, Josh Hosteler, Nello Fossi, Ben Dicken, and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-Upon arriving onsite the Department spoke to Shane Kriebel. Mr. Kriebel stated that an explosion of the production tank had occurred while the well tender was blowing out the well, at approximately 9:40 am. Mr. Kriebel stated they believe the explosion was caused by a faulty or damaged grounding wire. He stated that approximately 10 barrels of an oil and brine mixture was released. He stated that remediation was underway and that they would be following Act 2 for this clean up. He stated that saw dust and roughly 4 bags of Oil Gator were used to soak up any standing and pooled brine/oil in order to prevent further leaching in to the ground and easier excavation. He stated they had installed booms in the ditch behind the well site to prevent further migration of the released oil and brine.The Department's observations are as follows:At the time of the Department's arrival, the Department observed an area roughly 40 feet around the production equipment that appeared heavily saturated with an orange tinted fluid, presumably an oil and brine mixture. The Department observed what appeared to be the bottom portion of the production tank on the ground near the rest of the production equipment. A light-colored powder(Oil Gator) was observed placed on the ground in the area where the production tank previously was. A ditch that extended along the western perimeter of the well site, and down slope near the southern perimeter was observed. There appeared to be released fluid in this ditch directly behind the production equipment area, as well as in the ditch downslope on the southern perimeter totaling roughly 120 feet of ditch that appeared to be impacted. 2 booms and hay bales were observed installed in the ditch, one approximately 25 feet north of the production equipment, and one approximately 70 feet downslope south of the production equipment.The Department then began to obtain conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment as well as in the ditch. Conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment were OR (over of detectable range, over 20mS), in approximately a 25 foot radius in which readings then appeared to be comparable to background readings of 0.16mS. Conductivity readings in the ditch were also OR, however readings appear to become comparable to the background reading near the northern boom installed with a reading taken at the boom of 0.19mS. Readings at the southern boom installed were OR, with readings taken approximately 15 feet downslope of the southern boom of 13.23mS. The Department recommended to Mr.Kriebel that additional measures be taken to prevent the migration of contaminates downslope. Mr. Kriebel then had an additional boom installed downslope of the previously installed one on the southern perimeter.

Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Other water puddles tested at less than 0.6 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance fluids with Chesapeake's Kyle Stephens. He directed an arriving vac truck to start sucking up the fluids. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for flowback/production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks in secondary containment that were connected to the wellheads. There were 10 frac tanks on the north side of location that were stationed in secondary containment but were not connected to the well heads at the time of the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface while cleaning up after fracking operations were completed and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The release of a large volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Continue to monitor the areas with temporary stabilization and apply addition resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 1010 hours.

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-01
Comments: Brian Ayers of DEP was contacted by MSL's Dick Pascarella on 4/23/2020 regarding a condensate leak from a tank that was found that day. PA Fish and Boat Commission officer Tom Mcmann was on site 4/24/2020 to follow up and took some photos that are included in this report. It appears as though a small, uncontained drip gas tank had a failure at a fitting at some point prior to the spill being found. This tank holds mostly water that condenses from the gas coming from the compressor station nearby, but also contains some condensed petroleum liquids. An estimated 5-10 gallons of this fluid escaped from the broken fitting and was spilled to the ground. Some of this ran down slope toward an UNT of Chappel Fork, with some collecting in a low, wet area and a small amount eventually entering the water. Tom Mcmann documented photos of the condensate in the vernal pool area, which is included in the attached photos. A Department site visit was performed 5/1/2020. The operator has scraped up the surface of the contaminated site, and placed down straw mulch and seed. They also put down gravel around equipment close to the stream and have built containment around the drip gas tank. The area close to the stream was observed to have a strong condensate odor and some sheen could be spotted entering the stream when this area was agitated on the stream banks. Some product was noted, mostly in the form of sheen, in the UNT Chappel Fork. The stream crosses Chappel Fork Rd a few feet from where the product entered, and sheen was visible upon agitation approximately 150-200 feet downstream. No free product was apparent and no other waters were impacted. The operator was contacted and instructed to place booms for containment and monitor through the weekend, followed by a run of agitating the stream bottom to push any product caught in the substrate to collect it in the next week. They also dug up the impacted soil next to the stream with shovels and removed it. Bill Otto of MSL sent photos to show that booms were placed and digging done as of late Friday, May 1. Further followup will be done as possible.

Comments: On 07/15/2025, a Drilling inspection was conducted at the MINGO WELL SITE in Union Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) andPreparedness, Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan was present in mailbox (Photo 1).-The well site entrance and access road appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues observed (Photo 2 and 3).-I observed active construction for NINFS004 pipeline along the Mingo limit of disturbance (LOD).Overall, well pad slope and sound wall appeared to be in stable condition (Photo 4 and 5).-Secondary containment was observed throughout well site. Falcon 25 drilling rig, well casings, equipment, drill cuttings were observed within containment. Trucks were onsite to remove impaired water (Photo 6-18).-I observed multiple wet spots along the west side of the drilling secondary containment and throughout the travel lane. I utilized a Field Scout Conductivity probe to observe numerous elevated and over range readings within a 180x70 ft section. The Department contacted Environmental EQT Logan Dominick to notify them of the spill found. I observed the elevated fluid was spread out throughout the well pad within the 180 x 70 ft section. It appears the spill is greater than 42 gallons (Photo 19-25)-The Department reported the spill to EQT Logan Dominick on 07/15/2025 at 9:30 AM. EQT submitted the incident to the Department on 07/15/2025 at 10:40 AM. (CTS 390645)Determination:The operator failed to report the release of impaired fluid with compliance of 78.66 until after the Department inspected and found the spill. Additional photos and documentation are on inspection 2 and 3. Violations are being issued for impaired fluid found by the Department and spilled onto well pad: 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 78a.66(b)(2)

Comments: The inspection is being conducted in response to a spill reported by Chevron on 12/5/2019. Aqueous and soil samples are being collected in addition to the inspection. More of the secondary containment has been removed since the previous inspection. The pad smells strongly of petroleum. Chevron representative Gene Barchetti is present on site. Additional breaches in secondary containment are now visible. Multiple areas around and between the well heads, and to the south of the the well heads, have significant quantities of drilling mud and/or staining (Photos #1, 2, 3, 6, 7, and 8). Larger quantities of stormwater have been contaminated than previously observed. Stormwater discharging from under secondary containment still in place south of the well heads has a rainbow sheen (Photo #4); the large puddle below this discharge also has a sheen (Photo #3). Gene Barchetti was shown the discharge and the sheen. Stormwater has transported and concentrated drilling mud to the NE corner of the pad (Photo #5) and into a stormwater channel downslope. Both the NE pad corner and downslope in the stormwater channel have the strongest petroleum smell encountered on the site. Multiple pieces of equipment not in use remain without secondary containment. A significant portion of secondary containment remains. The Department requests photographic documentation of conditions under the remaining containment obtained during removal activities. Based on the 5 barrel release estimate in the Initial Report of Incident as documented in Inspection Record #2971125 and evidence gathered and reported in this inspection and Inspection Record #2970703, the Department recommends remediating the spill pursuant to 78a66(c)(2).

Permit API: 083-56748
Unconventional: Yes
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/02/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Jeff Passerrello, of Seneca Resources, to Brian Ayers, WQS Supervisor with the Department, on July 1, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred near West Branch Pad 0.It was reported that approximately a total of 15 gallons of diesel fuel was released on the roadway while filling a fuel cell near the access road for West Branch Pad 0. The incident occurred at 41.6036786, -78.4552038. Upon arrival to the site, a work crew was actively shoveling contaminated material from the roadway into containment. The released fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred and remained on the road. A PID meter was used to verify the removal of all the contaminated material. Tighe Truman, a representative from Seneca Resources, was on site at the time of the inspection. He inferred the contaminated waste would be tested and taken to a local landfill to be properly disposed of. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chesapeake Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-20
Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 886080
Permit API: 131-20561
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-29
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (5)wells on the HUNTER pad. The HUNTER 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a temporary poly vent tank via rubber lines. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - The (20x13) annulus vents of the 21HC and 22HC were opened within first 12 hrs. of PBUT due to pressures exceeding 35 psi.These vents were shut back in @ 7 am this morning, check @ 9 am showed pressures over 100 psi. on (20x13) annuli of both the 21HC and the 22HC wells. Op. Rep. bled down these annuli pressures below 30 psi. for remainder of PBUT's. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2017-03-07 to Eqt Production Co in Morgan Twp, Greene county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Eqt Production Co
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2017-03-07
Violation Code 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID 780210
Permit API 059-25377
Unconventional Y
County Greene
Municipality Morgan Twp
Inspection Type Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date 2017-03-07
Comments On 03/06/16 a complaint was received by the Department alleging BMP failures at the Hildebrand well site. On 03/07/17 at approximately 1330 hours I, along with Water Quality Specialist Supervisor John Carson, conducted a complaint inspection of the site. The Act 9 sign was in place and all required documents were present. Gravel from the site was found across Bowser Road. This is a violation of 102.5(m)(4) for impacts outside of the limits of disturbance. A black corrugated pipe that was not shown on the E&S plans was observed on the right side of the access road immediately upon entry to the site. It is requested that EQT provide information on this pipe in the NOV response. The rain garden was not functioning as designed and is at risk of failure. Water was bypassing the riser structure and draining through the soils between the rain garden toward the channel near the stilling well. A significant amount of sediment was observed in the rain garden and sediment laden water was observed in the stilling well. The second culvert up the access road at elevation 1060 was causing significant erosion and sediment discharge to the pond on the UNT to Castile Run. The silt sock at the discharge point of the culvert was placed on top of rip rap, preventing the sock from functioning. Extensive erosion was observed on the western side of the site. Erosion extended from the rip rap channel adjacent to the western side of the well pad into the location of the removed sediment trap. Multiple erosion channels were observed. Site BMPs were not properly maintained and water had undercut the silt socks. The final sock before leaving the LOD was covered in sediment and sediment and water were passing over top of the sock. Additional erosion was observed at the rip rap channel at the far western end of the site. Due to the erosion from the western side of the site, sediment laden water was entering the UNT to Castile run and the pond off site. The pond was not indicated on the E&S plan. A significant amount of sediment and rock from the site was observed in the pond. The deposition of the sediment and rock had created an obstruction similar to a sand bar. Along the border between the fence between the western side of the well site and the pipeline an orange safety fence was observed that appeared to be partially buried. It is highly recommended that the safety fence be removed. A small slide was observed on the south eastern side of the slope between the well pad and the channel leading to the rain garden. It is highly recommended that the slide be inspected and repaired to prevent risk to the well pad. An erosion channel was observed from the north eastern corner of the pad toward the channel. It is recommended this be repaired.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2026
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8266305
Permit API: 125-28285
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2026
Comments: Inspection Report 1 of 2On 03/03/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the John Hunter Well Site in Donegal Township, Washington County (37-125-28285). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio (PA DEP).The following was observed:-Act 9 sign (Photo 1).-Sediment-laden water flowing from access road and site to culvert inlet (Photos 2-4). Recommend access road maintenance.-Culvert inlet pipe receiving road fines and sediment-laden water (Photos 5,6).-Culvert outlet area appears to be pooling/discharging sediment; visible from access road (Photos 7,8). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Accelerated erosion flow path downslope from culvert outlet (Photos 9-11).-Existing Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears overtaken by wood debris and vegetation; sediment deposition from what appears to be significant flow downslope (Photos 12,13). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Flow path of sediment-laden water continued downslope (Photos 14-16).-Sediment deposit concentrated area (Photos 17,18).-Flow path of sediment-laden water discharging into unnamed tributary flowing to Little Wheeling Creek (Photos 19,20).-Further down access road toward pad, culvert inlet and outlet related to inspection report 2 of 2 appears receiving and discharging sediment-laden water; accelerated erosion and sediment flow path downslope into wooded area offsite (Photos 21,22).Range Resources Environmental Compliance Specialist Dennis Furmanek was contacted on 03/04/2026 regarding observations noted above.Recommendations as noted above.Due to the discharge of sediment from the site capable of reaching waters of the Commonwealth and failure to minimize accelerated erosion and sedimentation, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78a.53, 102.4(b)4, 102.11(A)2, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.
